title: Measuring the actual impact of AI coding | Abi Noda from DX
summary: DX's Abi Noda on measuring AI coding: ~3 hours/week self-reported savings, weak link to throughput, engagement gains, top-down pressure, and bottlenecks shifting outside coding.

assertions.quote: On average developers report saving about three hours per week thanks AI tools.
we're not seeing that strong of a correlation in terms of something like you know code throughput
even with a pretty high acceleration of the coding part of the job. you you're kind of limited by these other factors
one of the strongest relationships we're seeing in the data is actually with engagement meaning developer job engagement
they believe is more fear driven than utility uh utility driven

verdicts.note: Anecdotal report from vendor researchers; motivation for adoption has not been measured.

METR Feb 2026: more developers refused to work without AI, and 30-50% held back tasks, which METR attributes mainly to higher expectations of AI uplift (plus lower pay). Developer quotes describe liking the tools, not fear of obsolescence.
